title: How to Remove Your Number From Truecaller
html:
Unlisting is a request you make to Truecaller, and it only hides your number from its directory. It does not stop spam calls, and it does not remove you from other caller-ID services. Follow Truecaller's own current instructions for the steps. This page tells you what to check before you start, how to confirm it worked, and what to do if you want your data erased.

Last updated: 10 Oct 2026. Truecaller changes its screens and forms, so always use the current official page.

I read Truecaller's unlisting page on 10 Oct 2026. I did not unlist my own number to test it.

1. Decide whether you want to unlist

Unlist if you do not want your name shown to people who search your number. Think twice if you take calls from strangers for work, because being identified can help them trust the call. Unlisting is about visibility, not about blocking calls.

2. The steps

Truecaller's unlisting page asks you to enter your phone number and confirm, and says it can take up to 24 hours before the number is removed. Before you confirm, the page lists what you lose: unlisting can't be reversed, people won't know when you are calling, you get no spam protection and caller identification, no one-tap sign-in on third-party apps, and no Call Reason to find out why someone is calling.

3. Check that it worked

  • Wait for the time Truecaller states, then search your number from a device or account that is not yours.
  • Ask someone who has your number saved to search it in their app.
  • Check again after a month, and after a few months.

What unlisting does not do

  • It does not stop spam or scam calls. For that, use the blocking and reporting tools in our spam call guide, and report fraud on Sanchar Saathi.
  • It does not remove your number from other caller-ID apps or data sites. Each has its own process.
  • It is a request to the company. It does not force deletion of the data it holds about you.

Asking for erasure under India's DPDP law

India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 gives a person ("data principal") rights over their personal data. The government notified the DPDP Rules, 2025, and PIB's summary lists these rights: to access, to correct, to erase, to file a grievance, and to nominate someone to act for you. The rules take effect in phases, with some provisions in force at once and others after 12 and after 18 months, so check which rights apply on the day you read this.

If you want your data erased, not just hidden, ask the company in writing, in the way its privacy notice describes, and keep a copy of your request.

What to do next

  1. Follow Truecaller's current unlisting steps and note the date.
  2. Check again after a month.
  3. Use call blocking for spam. Unlisting will not do that.
